rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Art as a spiritual path", "body": "Chance traced his road to InnerVerse back to a college class on writing the spiritual journey, which reopened questions he had shut down after losing his faith in his late teens. Music festivals followed, where he met people living by their creativity and realized that the only gap between us and our heroes is time and effort. He framed aptitude as passion, and care as the conduit that moves energy through every system, and said that became the founding scope of the show: art as a way to liberate yourself from suffering."}, {"title": "The dark arts and the beauty way", "body": "Chance described a recent plot twist in his thinking: not all art serves humanity, and artifice can work against nature, as the word pharmacy, traced to a Greek root tied to sorcery, hints. Kerri offered the beauty way, a life lived in harmony with nature's cycles of birth, flourishing, release and death. Chance answered with the vulture, whose beauty lies in its harmony rather than its looks, since it turns rotting carrion into one of the most sterile compounds known to science."}, {"title": "Perception and the original light", "body": "Picking up Kerri's reading of gene key 11, Chance proposed an inverted model of perception. Rather than the brain stitching together signals that arrive at different speeds, he suggested the third eye takes in undifferentiated source light while the amygdala decides how much of it you can handle. That light is split through the thalamus and routed to the senses, which act as filters rather than detectors. In this view nothingness is inseparable from somethingness, and the void and the clear light of source are one."}, {"title": "Aperture, death and the ancestral field", "body": "Kerri said she would rather not see the entities she clears, and Chance called this aperture: something you are in charge of, which can open to one spectrum and stay closed to another. He spoke about owning your death as the final moment to choose who you are. Drawing on Eileen Day McKusick's biofield anatomy, he described an ancestral field reaching out like tree rings, mother's line on the right and father's on the left, where old obstructions distort the light we project outward."}, {"title": "The unbegotten self and false valuation", "body": "Chance said he is over beginnings and endings and sees creator and creation as one eternal process, a verb rather than a noun. Genetic continuity, he suggested, gives the unbegotten self a reference point in the void, like a save point in a video game. Turning to Kerri's concern about homelessness in Texas, he argued that debt-based money turns society into a game of musical chairs, and that calling part of source a resource, or a living being a legal person, is how false valuation takes hold."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: I joined Kerri Hummingbird on her Soul Nectar Show on Valentine's Day 2021, snowed in, for an unplanned conversation that wandered from art as a spiritual path to the third eye, nothingness, the ancestral biofield and the debt-based money system.
